questions.stem: A man is on trial for assault. The prosecution presents a witness who testifies under oath that she saw the accused strike the victim with a metal rod during an argument. There is no video footage, no fingerprints on the weapon, and no DNA evidence linking the accused to the crime scene. However, the witness insists she saw the incident clearly from across the street. What type of evidence does the witness’s testimony constitute?

Dr. Smith, a licensed surgeon, works at City Hospital as an independent contractor. During a private procedure in his own clinic, which does not belong to the hospital’s facilities, he negligently injures a patient. The patient sues both Dr. Smith and City Hospital. Which statement is correct regarding the hospital’s liability?

options.label: A
options.text: City Hospital is liable because Dr. Smith uses its name.

options.label: B
options.text: City Hospital is liable due to vicarious liability for Dr. Smith’s negligence.

options.label: C
options.text: City Hospital is not liable because Dr. Smith acted outside the scope of hospital employment.

options.label: D
options.text: City Hospital is not liable because Dr. Smith had malpractice insurance.

questions.answerText: City Hospital is not liable because Dr. Smith acted outside the scope of hospital employment.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) City Hospital is not liable because Dr. Smith acted outside the scope of hospital employment.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old individual diagnosed with schizophrenia commits an act that would otherwise be considered a criminal offense. The act was committed during a period of acute psychotic episode. The individual's medical history indicates sporadic adherence to prescribed antipsychotic medication. Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding the criminal responsibility of mentally ill?

options.label: A
options.text: Accused will be responsible since the act was committed while not adhering to prescribed medication.

options.label: B
options.text: Accused will not be responsible as the offence was committed during psychotic episode, regardless of medication adherence.

options.label: C
options.text: Accused will be responsible due to the sporadic nature of the individual's symptoms.

options.label: D
options.text: The accused will not be responsible only if the act was committed during a state of complete unconsciousness.

questions.answerText: Accused will not be responsible as the offence was committed during psychotic episode, regardless of medication adherence.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) The accused will not be responsible as the offence was committed during psychotic episode, regardless of medication adherence

questions.stem: In a case of death due to alleged poisoning, the prosecution presents a toxicology expert who testifies that the victim’s body had toxic substance based on the analysis of the stomach contents. The defence argues that the expert’s testimony should be inadmissible as toxicology expert neither examined the victim while he was alive, nor he conducted the autopsy himself. Which of the below is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The toxicology expert’s testimony is inadmissible because they did not have first-hand knowledge of the victim’s condition at the time of death.

options.label: B
options.text: The toxicology testimony is admissible as it is based on expert opinion, not on first-hand knowledge.

options.label: C
options.text: The forensic expert’s testimony is admissible only if it can be corroborated by a common witness who had first-hand knowledge of the victim’s condition.

questions.answerText: The toxicology testimony is admissible as it is based on expert opinion, not on first-hand knowledge.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) The toxicology testimony is admissible as it is based on expert opinion, not on first-hand knowledge.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old intelligence officer is undergoing screening to ensure loyalty and integrity before receiving a high-security clearance. Investigators decide to use a method based on measuring brain recognition signals, which is unaffected by emotional reactions. Which of the following best differentiates brain fingerprinting from polygraph testing?

options.label: A
options.text: Brain fingerprinting measures heart rate variability.

options.label: C
options.text: Brain fingerprinting detects cognitive memory-based responses.

options.label: D
options.text: Brain fingerprinting determines truthfulness through galvanic skin response.

questions.answerText: Brain fingerprinting detects cognitive memory-based responses.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Brain fingerprinting detects cognitive memory-based responses

questions.stem: A forensic science student is examining a case study where a body exhibited an unusual glow during the postmortem examination. The instructor explains that this phenomenon, known as postmortem luminescence, can be caused by specific types of bacteria. Which bacteria are known to produce Postmortem Luminescence?
Which of the following is true with respect to dribbling of saliva in hanging?

options.label: A
options.text: Dribbling of saliva occurs in antemortem hanging and on same side of ligature knot. It does not occur in ligature strangulation

options.label: B
options.text: Dribbling of saliva occurs in antemortem hanging and opposite to side of ligature knot. It does not occur in ligature strangulation

options.label: C
options.text: Dribbling of saliva occurs in both antemortem hanging and ligature strangulation, opposite to side of ligature knot.

options.label: D
options.text: Dribbling of saliva occurs in both antemortem hanging and ligature strangulation, on same side of ligature knot.

questions.answerText: Dribbling of saliva occurs in antemortem hanging and opposite to side of ligature knot. It does not occur in ligature strangulation
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Dribbling of saliva occurs in antemortem hanging and opposite to side of ligature knot. It does not occur in ligature strangulation

questions.stem: What is the primary cause of Paltauf's haemorrhages in drowning?

options.label: A
options.text: Direct trauma to the lungs from water entry

options.label: B
options.text: Rupture of alveolar walls due to increased pressure during forced expirations

options.label: C
options.text: Inhalation of foreign particles leading to lung irritation

options.label: D
options.text: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to water aspiration

questions.answerText: Rupture of alveolar walls due to increased pressure during forced expirations
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Rupture of alveolar walls due to increased pressure during forced expirations

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the effect of environmental temperature on rigor mortis is most accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: In hot environments, rigor mortis sets in slowly because the body’s metabolic processes are slowed down.

options.label: B
options.text: In cold environments, rigor mortis sets in slowly because the body’s metabolic processes are slowed down

options.label: C
options.text: In cold environments, rigor mortis persist for more time due to faster decomposition

options.label: D
options.text: In hot environments, rigor mortis persist for more time due to faster decomposition

questions.answerText: In cold environments, rigor mortis sets in slowly because the body’s metabolic processes are slowed down
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) In cold environments, rigor mortis sets in slowly because the body’s metabolic processes are slowed down

questions.stem: The Spalding sign, characterized by the overlapping of cranial bones in a fetus after intrauterine death, is primarily caused by:

options.label: A
options.text: Severe maternal hypertension leading to intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR)

options.label: B
options.text: Brain ischemia leading to intrauterine death

options.label: C
options.text: Shrinkage of the cerebrum after death, leading to loss of alignment and overriding of cranial bones

options.label: D
options.text: A genetic anomaly causing cranial bone malformation

questions.answerText: Shrinkage of the cerebrum after death, leading to loss of alignment and overriding of cranial bones
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. C) Shrinkage of the cerebrum after death leading to loss of alignment and overriding of cranial bones.

options.text: Heat stiffening due to ATP depletion

options.label: B

options.label: C

questions.stemHtml: Police officer brings a 15-year-old male child to doctor for medical examination. Mother of the child gives the history that his uncle has been sexual assaulting him for past 2 years, which she came to know now and complained the police. Doctor examines the anus, which shows features as in the picture below. It is suggestive of?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Repeated anal sex with child

questions.stem: A forensic expert conducts a Lugol's iodine test on an accused's glans penis during an examination 48 hours after an alleged sexual assault. The filter paper turns brownish. What does this color change indicate, and why does this reaction occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Presence of smegma, indicating no sexual activity within the last 24 hours.

options.label: B
options.text: Presence of glycogen in vaginal cells, indicating possible sexual activity within the last 4 days.

options.label: C
options.text: Reaction to urinary residue, indicating recent urination.

options.label: D
options.text: Absence of cleaning, indicating poor personal hygiene.

questions.answerText: Presence of glycogen in vaginal cells, indicating possible sexual activity within the last 4 days.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Presence of glycogen in vaginal cells, indicating possible sexual activity within the last 4 days.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true with respect to examination of a female victim of sexual assault?

options.label: A
options.text: Toluidine dye should be used to detect recent microinjuries on genitalia before taking the swab for sperm detection

options.label: B
options.text: History should not be taken from the victim if her age < 12 years

options.label: C

options.label: D

questions.solutionHtml: Ans. D) Per speculum examination may not be needed in young victim if there is no history of penetration

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after consuming a large amount of locally brewed alcohol. questions.stemHtml: In a case involving suspected chemical exposure, an autopsy reveals extensive skin discoloration as seen in the image. What can be the likely mechanism?

options.label: B
options.text: Deep tissue liquefactive necrosis by nitric acid

options.label: C

questions.answerText: Reaction of nitric acid with amino acids in the skin
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Reaction of nitric acid with amino acids in the skin

questions.stem: In cyanide poisoning, the characteristic cherry red discoloration of the skin is best explained by:

options.label: A
options.text: Accumulation of oxygenated hemoglobin as cells are not able to use oxygen

options.label: B
options.text: Increased carboxyhemoglobin due to carbon monoxide production

options.label: C
options.text: Cyanide binding to hemoglobin, enhancing oxygen affinity

options.label: D
options.text: Formation of a cyanide-cytochrome c oxidase complex with a cherry red color

questions.answerText: Accumulation of oxygenated hemoglobin as cells are not able to use oxygen
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Accumulation of oxygenated hemoglobin as cells are not able to use oxygen

questions.stem: Which of the following substances of abuse has effects that are most similar to those of cocaine?

Identify which of the following statements are true regarding the materials required for forensic analysis of specific poisons: Vitreous humor is commonly examined for alcohol poisoning.The skin is analyzed for decomposition in cases of strychnine poisoning.Brain tissue is essential for detecting organophosphate poisoning.Fatty tissue is primarily used for examining pesticides and insecticides.
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Only 1, 3, and 4 are true

questions.stemHtml: What is a Woronoff ring associated with, in the context of psoriasis?

questions.stemHtml: An elderly man develops itchy plaques that rapidly evolve into tense bullae on his lower limbs. The blisters are firm and do not rupture easily. questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Basement membrane zone destruction

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with joint stiffness, fatigue, low-grade fever, and a photosensitive facial rash. Which of the following drugs used as nail lacquer belongs to the morpholine class of antifungal agents?

A 52-year-old patient is scheduled for a routine orthopedic surgery under general anesthesia. The anesthesiologist opts to use desflurane as the primary inhaled anesthetic agent. While discussing its properties with a trainee, the anesthesiologist reviews several characteristics of desflurane. Which one of the following statements regarding desflurane is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It causes severe effects on kidney

options.label: B
options.text: It is structural analogue of isoflurane

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman is scheduled for a brief outpatient endoscopic procedure under monitored anesthesia care in a day-care setting. She requires adequate intraoperative analgesia but must recover quickly after the procedure to be discharged home the same day. The anesthesiologist must choose an opioid that provides effective pain control while allowing rapid postoperative recovery with minimal residual sedation. Which opioid is most suitable for intraoperative analgesia in this scenario?

A 45-year-old male with a history of chronic atrial fibrillation is scheduled for a total knee arthroplasty. He is currently managed on warfarin therapy, which has been held for the past 5 days. Preoperative labs show a platelet count of 65,000/mm³, and he reports taking aspirin 75 mg up until two days ago. He does not have a history of bleeding disorders, and intravenous heparin has been considered for bridging warfarin. Considering his medication history and lab findings, which of the following would generally not be a contraindication to performing central neuraxial anesthesia in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. B) Recent use of aspirin

questions.stem: A 30-year-old construction worker presents to the pain clinic for a procedure involving local anesthetic infiltration for pain management. The physician wants to ensure that the patient receives adequate anesthesia with minimal systemic absorption issues. What is the correct order of routes for the absorption of local anesthetics from fastest to slowest?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Intercostal, Brachial, Epidural, Caudal

questions.stem: A medical student studying the materials used in anesthesia is examining the components of soda lime, a CO2 absorbent utilized during surgeries to remove carbon dioxide from breathing circuits. During a cesarean section under spinal anesthesia, a patient experiences a significant drop in blood pressure and tachycardia. Which of the following is the primary mechanism causing this?

options.label: A
options.text: Increased cardiac output due to sympathetic stimulation

options.label: B
options.text: Blockade of parasympathetic nerve fibers leading to increased heart rate

questions.stem: A 74-year-old alcoholic undergoing hip replacement under general anesthesia is maintained on sevoflurane. Midway through surgery, his BIS drops to 40 and his BP falls to 70/40 mmHg. His MAC is 1.0. What is the most likely reason for excessive anesthetic depth in this patient?

options.text: Age-related decrease in minimum alveolar concentration (MAC)

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Increased MAC requirement due to chronic alcohol use

options.label: D
options.text: Intraoperative awareness causing paradoxical BIS drop

questions.answerText: Age-related decrease in minimum alveolar concentration (MAC)
